javascript-1.title: Getting started with the language
javascript-1.goal: Start with variables and understand one small concept at a time.
javascript-1.checkpoint: Use a function, a loop and a condition to total the study minutes in a lessons array.

javascript-2.title: Understand data and scope
javascript-2.goal: Transform collections, validate input, and understand bindings and built-in utilities.
javascript-2.checkpoint: Explain a closure and build a validated calculation with no accidental string concatenation.

javascript-3.title: Build interactions in the browser
javascript-3.goal: Learn HTML/CSS structure before you manipulate the DOM.
javascript-3.checkpoint: Build a keyboard-accessible list whose actions are handled through delegation.

javascript-4.title: Understand objects and design
javascript-4.goal: Understand the this receiver and prototypes before the OOP project.
javascript-4.checkpoint: Explain this at three call sites and implement a small state-machine project.

javascript-5.title: Handle async work and delivery
javascript-5.goal: Move from promises and fetch to concurrency limits and modules.
javascript-5.checkpoint: Handle a failed request, cap the active work, and explain how the app is delivered to the browser.

javascript-6.title: Verify how the code behaves
javascript-6.goal: Verify your modules and async knowledge with repeatable tests and a debugging workflow.
javascript-6.checkpoint: Run boundary tests and a controlled async failure case, then explain the regression.

javascript-7.title: Understand persistence and collaboration
javascript-7.goal: Practise the local data lifecycle, offline conflicts and reviewed Git changes.
javascript-7.checkpoint: Explain a two-tab conflict policy and the exact meaning of a staged versus unstaged diff.

react-1.title: Understand components first
react-1.goal: Start with JSX and props, then learn state, rendering and identity.
react-1.checkpoint: In an editable list, keep each draft attached to the correct item.

react-2.title: Reuse UI and synchronize safely
react-2.goal: After composition, learn effects, refs and custom hooks.
react-2.checkpoint: Extract a reusable component and clean up a cancellable effect.

react-3.title: Assemble a complete application
react-3.goal: Add navigation, shared state, a server cache and typed boundaries.
react-3.checkpoint: Build a routed page with a clear cache identity and validated API data.

react-4.title: Measure, then practise
react-4.goal: Profile production behaviour before machine coding.
react-4.checkpoint: Show stale-request protection, keyboard behaviour and one measured improvement.

react-5.title: Test the user journey
react-5.goal: Check the observable contracts of forms, async screens and accessibility.
react-5.checkpoint: Write a form test with accessible queries and separately identify the browser-only checks.

react-native-1.title: The foundation of native UI
react-native-1.goal: Understand the Expo workflow, core components and mobile layout.
react-native-1.checkpoint: Inspect a safe-area-aware screen on Android and iOS.

react-native-2.title: Lists and screen navigation
react-native-2.goal: Connect virtualized data with the route lifecycle.
react-native-2.checkpoint: Verify a deep link from the list to a detail screen, and the back behaviour.

react-native-3.title: Forms, data and device features
react-native-3.goal: Handle input, offline state, storage and permissions.
react-native-3.checkpoint: Show a usable recovery for a denied permission and a failed request.

react-native-4.title: Measure, test and release
react-native-4.goal: Understand performance, accessibility and compatible releases.
react-native-4.checkpoint: Explain the release checklist and the boundary between an OTA update and a native build.

java-1.title: Write your first Java program
java-1.goal: Run main, declare variables, make decisions, and create methods and instances.
java-1.checkpoint: Compile a learner program with two independent objects and an array-processing method.

java-2.title: Build a reliable core model
java-2.goal: On top of basic classes, build OOP, collections, exceptions, streams and memory reasoning.
java-2.checkpoint: Choose a suitable collection, preserve the equality contract and close an owned resource.

java-3.title: Build, test and save data
java-3.goal: Set up builds and tests before database and SQL concurrency.
java-3.checkpoint: Test a JDBC operation; explain a join and an atomic inventory update.

java-4.title: Understand concurrency and resource limits
java-4.goal: Learn thread safety, virtual threads and bounded resources.
java-4.checkpoint: Show a race-safe operation and explain why backpressure is needed.

java-5.title: Evolve types, schema and object design
java-5.goal: Practise finite variants, metadata, compatible migrations and invariant-based low-level design.
java-5.checkpoint: Verify the contract of an immutable model, a safe migration and a concurrent loan claim.

spring-boot-1.title: Start and configure the application
spring-boot-1.goal: Understand Boot startup, bean wiring and typed config.
spring-boot-1.checkpoint: Start the app and diagnose a missing bean or an invalid setting.

spring-boot-2.title: Build a clear HTTP boundary
spring-boot-2.goal: Build REST endpoints with DTOs, validation and controlled errors.
spring-boot-2.checkpoint: Show the documented responses for a successful creation and for rejected input.

spring-boot-3.title: Save and secure business operations
spring-boot-3.goal: Apply transactions, persistence and authorization boundaries.
spring-boot-3.checkpoint: Prove that the invariant survives concurrent requests and that unauthorized access is rejected.

spring-boot-4.title: Verify and operate the service
spring-boot-4.goal: Test the boundaries, inspect telemetry and complete the deployment capstone.
spring-boot-4.checkpoint: Run the API acceptance cases and defend the recovery from a failed deployment.

spring-boot-5.title: Operate background work and caches
spring-boot-5.goal: Connect proxy boundaries, scheduled jobs and cache identity to failure scenarios.
spring-boot-5.checkpoint: Give a measurable contract for recovering from a duplicate job and a stale cache.

spring-boot-6.title: Trace the web runtime all the way down
spring-boot-6.goal: Connect servlet concurrency, forwarding and view rendering to Spring MVC.
spring-boot-6.checkpoint: Diagnose a shared request-field race and the loss of a redirect attribute.

spring-boot-7.title: Optional AI retrieval extension
spring-boot-7.goal: Understand authorized retrieval, evidence quality and the limits of model integration.
spring-boot-7.checkpoint: Give an evaluation contract for known, unsupported and unauthorized questions.

mongodb-1.title: Understand a server request
mongodb-1.goal: After Node and HTTP, learn Express routing and errors.
mongodb-1.checkpoint: Trace a request from the middleware to a controlled response.

mongodb-2.title: Model the data
mongodb-2.goal: Understand documents and CRUD before Mongoose schemas.
mongodb-2.checkpoint: Choose embedding or references from the actual read pattern, and validate writes.

mongodb-3.title: Write efficient queries
mongodb-3.goal: After indexes and aggregation, inspect plans and bounded streaming.
mongodb-3.checkpoint: Explain the winning plan of a tenant query and stream a large export.

mongodb-4.title: Secure it, then deploy
mongodb-4.goal: Add authentication and authorization before payments, uploads and deployment.
mongodb-4.checkpoint: Reject unauthorized access and recover safely from a duplicate webhook.

mongodb-5.title: Verify the API lifecycle
mongodb-5.goal: Practise real HTTP testing, database isolation and bounded shutdown.
mongodb-5.checkpoint: Run a parallel-safe request test and the acceptance cases for an in-flight shutdown.

dsa-1.title: Understand cost and basic structures
dsa-1.goal: Before patterns, learn complexity, lists/stacks/queues and hashing.
dsa-1.checkpoint: Choose an array, a queue or a map and justify the cost of the operation.

dsa-2.title: Learn reusable problem-solving patterns
dsa-2.goal: After counters, pointers and search, study recursion and sorting.
dsa-2.checkpoint: Before coding, trace the binary-search invariant and a recursive call.

dsa-3.title: Understand ordered candidates and hierarchy
dsa-3.goal: Apply the stack invariant, then learn trees and heaps, and after that graphs.
dsa-3.checkpoint: Prove the complexity bound of a stack and implement a heap-based top-k.

dsa-4.title: Solve graphs and DP
dsa-4.goal: Use queues, recursion, hashing and heaps to understand dependencies and repeated subproblems.
dsa-4.checkpoint: Choose between BFS and Dijkstra, then derive a DP state and recurrence.

dsa-5.title: Prove the advanced choices
dsa-5.goal: Learn greedy and interval proofs, and trie, bitmask and range-query structures.
dsa-5.checkpoint: Compare a greedy solution against a brute-force oracle and trace a Fenwick update.

system-design-1.title: The common foundation of design
system-design-1.goal: Make requirements and capacity clear before you choose scaling or a cache.
system-design-1.checkpoint: Write down the workload, latency, freshness and correctness assumptions.

system-design-2.title: Understand React frontend architecture
system-design-2.goal: Design rendering, state and performance before the frontend case.
system-design-2.checkpoint: Build an accessible catalog with URL state, a cache and stale-request handling.

system-design-3.title: Understand Java backend architecture
system-design-3.goal: After API and data boundaries, study messaging, reliability and operations.
system-design-3.checkpoint: Explain the reservation invariant, the retry identity and a failure timeline.

system-design-4.title: Work through end-to-end case studies
system-design-4.goal: Study both sides and combine frontend and backend reasoning.
system-design-4.checkpoint: Trace the flow that preserves durable state through a checkout or reconnect failure.

system-design-5.title: Defend distributed guarantees and API contracts
system-design-5.goal: Compare read consistency, global limits and API styles against the workload and failure history.
system-design-5.checkpoint: Define the expected outcomes for replica lag, a limiter outage and a batch lookup failure.

system-design-6.title: Diagnose with OS and networking fundamentals
system-design-6.goal: Trace request latency through the process, memory, network and shared-resource layers.
system-design-6.checkpoint: Use evidence to separate a DNS/TCP/TLS failure, a pool wait and an unknown write outcome.

interview-1.title: Practise the language interview
interview-1.goal: Take the playbook for the language course you completed.
interview-1.checkpoint: Explain the output without looking at the answer and defend a design choice.

interview-2.title: Practise the application interview
interview-2.goal: Move from the language to frontend and database-backed scenarios.
interview-2.checkpoint: Complete one machine-coding or query-design drill, including its errors.

interview-3.title: Practise algorithms and architecture
interview-3.goal: Do these rounds after the related DSA or design course.
interview-3.checkpoint: State the invariant in coding and a measurable requirement in design.
